articles.title: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed to Be in Development at MachineGames
articles.summary: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames and franchise creators id Software confirmed what had long been rumored: that Wolfenstein 3 is in development. MachineGames will once again be developing it.
body: But now, Wolfenstein is back on the front burner at the Swedish studio. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at Machine Games," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed on X. "One of gaming’s most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more."

id Software and MachineGames added on to Sharma's post, which shows a page of the Wolfenstein 3 script, saying simply, "His reputation precedes him," referring to the action described on the script page. "Wolfenstein 3 is in production." The developers also confirmed that actors Brian Bloom (as B.J. Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (as Grace Walker) will return via a photo of the pair in the developer's motion-capture studio.

Wolfenstein 3 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Last year, in an interview with Noclip, MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson said the team had "always seen [BJ's story] as a trilogy," adding: "That journey for BJ, even during those first weeks at [id Software], when we mapped out New Order — we still had the plan for at least [BJ], what would happen in the second one and what would happen in the third one.

articles.title: Candy Crush Is Celebrating Xbox’s 25th Anniversary With Halo, Fallout, And Doom Crossovers, Including Remixed Music
articles.summary: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closures/divestitures, and game cancellations. But the celebrations are still going ahead, including an event from the Xbox-owned Candy Crush mobile game juggernaut.
body: Announced today, Candy Crush Saga is marking the Xbox anniversary with a "Game On" season that brings items and elements from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, Banjo-Kazooie, Crash Bandicoot, and Spyro into the game through a virtual pin-collection event. Additionally, the popular and recognizable music from some of those games is coming to Candy Crush in "unmistakable Candy style," developer King said.

The Game On event runs now through December 6. Players earn the themed pins, including Master Chief's iconic helmet, by progressing through Candy Crush's various levels throughout the season. The pins are being released physically, too, and people can enter a contest at the Candy Crush website for a chance to win.
In terms of the updated music, Candy Crush Saga is adding "Candyfied" versions of music from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, and Banjo-Kazooie.

You can check out a neat behind-the-scenes video below to see how composer Federico Truzzi worked with the developers at King to remix the songs with a Candy Crush flavor. The music was recorded by the German Film Orchestra Babelsberg and the Bulgarische Orthodoxe Chor Berlin e.V. choir.
points: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closures/divestitures, and game cancellations.

articles.title: A PlayStation 5 Compatible SSD With Heatsink Dropped to Possibly the Lowest Price We'll See for Black Friday
articles.summary: If you're an avid PS5 gamer, sooner or later you're going to need more storage. Grand Theft Auto 6, which comes out this month, will take up over 200GB of space alone. That's nearly 25% of your stock 1TB storage space, since a 1TB PS5 drive really equates to less than 850GB of usable storage.
body: Unfortunately, PlayStation storage deals are practically non-existent in 2026... but that changes today. Ahead of Black Friday, Walmart just dropped the price of the Verbatim Vi7000 1TB PlayStation 5 compatible solid state drive (SSD) to just $129 with free shipping. This is the lowest price I've seen for a high-speed 1TB SSD in months. If you want even more storage, the 2TB model is also on sale for $199. Both models even include a built-in heatsink. Never say never, but I think we'll be hard pressed to find a better price than this during Black Friday proper.

The Verbatim Vi7000 is Playstation 5 compatible. That means it fulfills all of Sony's requirements. It boasts sequential speeds of 7000MB/s read and 6500MB/s write, which easily surpasses the minimum recommended speed of 5,500MB/s. The SSD uses the PCI-Express Gen4x4 interface which slots neatly into the PS5's drive bay. It also has a preinstalled heatsink that will do a fine job of keeping your SSD cool.

Grand Theft Auto 6, which comes out this month, will take up over 200GB of space alone.

articles.title: Games Will Have A Physical Footprint Forever, Take-Two Boss Says, But It’ll Be “Very Small”
articles.summary: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gaming to go away entirely anytime soon, or ever, according to Take-Two's Strauss Zelnick.
body: He told The Game Business that it "may not be the end" for physical media entirely in games, even with Sony killing off PlayStation discs in 2028. He said there will "always be some physical business" for gaming, but it will be a "very small part of the business."
He likened the scale of it to the vinyl business for recorded music. Most people might stream music today, but the market for vinyl is still there--and it's growing.

For Take-Two, however, Zelnick said its business today is 98% digital. Going all-digital has a lot of benefits for publishers, but it's mainly about making more money. For GTA 6, the most highly anticipated game release ever, Rockstar is not offering the game on a disc, but the game will appear in stores via a code-in-a-box version.

GTA 6's $400 collector's edition comes with a range of physical goods (but not the game), and Rockstar is also releasing GTA 6's score on CD and vinyl, but the game itself remains a digital-only experience.
points: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gaming to go away entirely anytime soon, or ever, according to Take-Two's Strauss Zelnick.

articles.title: This Happy Ending For Two Games With Identical Names Was A Headache For Nintendo
articles.summary: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch. It's no coincidence, but the circumstances that led to this unusual situation certainly stem from a coincidence.
body: Publisher No More Robots launched Piece by Piece, a cozy sim game full of cute animal characters, on Steam back in March. Two days later, studio Neon Polygons self-published an unrelated puzzle-platformer where you jump through literal puzzle pieces that you connect together--this game is also called Piece by Piece.

What could have been a conflict between indie developers turned out to be the beginning of a wholesome business relationship. Both games were bundled together on Steam, and now No More Robots is publishing the Switch ports of both titles.

According to No More Robots co-founder Mike Rose, Neon Polygons "couldn't afford to bring their game to Switch," so No More Robots stepped in to publish the game for them. As with Steam, you can buy both games together in a bundle.

It's undeniably a heartwarming and unique story, though one would assume that having to figure out the logistics behind launching two games that not only have the same name, but the same release date and publisher as well, was a nightmare on the backend of the Nintendo eShop.
points: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch.
It's no coincidence, but the circumstances that led to this unusual situation certainly stem from a coincidence.

articles.title: Steam Makes Popular World War II Strategy Game Free to Play This Weekend
articles.summary: Steam regularly gives PC players an opportunity to try something new without spending a cent and these promotions are particularly useful for strategy fans, as they offer a chance to test out a new experience before deciding whether it's worth the investment.
body: One well-known World War II strategy franchise is joining the promotion this week, giving players four days to experience its latest mainline entry for free. Company of Heroes 3 is temporarily free to play on Steam until Nov. 16. And there's an additional incentive for anyone who decides to stick around the game with a 67% discount for a few more days after the free trial.

Developed by Relic Entertainment, Company of Heroes 3 is a real-time strategy game that takes players to the Mediterranean theater of World War II. Released in February 2023, it features two single-player campaigns alongside competitive multiplayer and cooperative modes.

Players can command different military factions, manage resources, construct bases, and lead infantry and armored units into battle. Its two campaigns take place across North Africa and Italy, with the Italian campaign featuring a dynamic map that gives players more freedom to approach the conflict. The game also offers several multiplayer factions, each with its own units and tactical options, making it a good fit for players who enjoy slower, more methodical battles that reward careful planning.

articles.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens’ Season 2 Release Date Announcement Includes Some Shocking Good News
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens spent its entire first season in the Haven of Ellora, but as the show's title makes clear, that's just one of many Havens spread across this post-apocalyptic landscape.
body: In Book 2, entitled ‘Discovery’, Pavi continues her chakra journey to the Floating Isles and learns more about what happened to Korra. Meanwhile, Nisha discovers vital information about the mysterious spirit energy Pavi released from Ellora. The girls are brought together in New Ba Sing Se, along with all their unresolved issues.

Throughout Book 1, Ellora was plagued by the Anomaly, a sort of spiritual affliction associated with fear that manifested as a diamond-shaped entity made of red energy. After a huge concentration of that energy exploded near Ellora, it created a large dome that threatened to consume the entire Haven. Only by unblocking her own root chakra was Pavi able to redirect the energy through her body and into the sky, where it manifested as an aurora. Based on a vision she received right after, another Haven called the Floating Isles needs her help. So at the end of Book 1, Pavi sets out into the Harshlands with Jae (Major Curda) at her side.

articles.title: Palworld developer Pocketpair gives employees time off for 'a 5-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches'
articles.summary: Amid the countless PTO requests and conspicuously-timed doctor appointment notices targeting November 19, one game studio's employees have been absolved of the need to provide themselves an alibi on Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day.
body: "On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," Pocketpair wrote in a memo announcing the company holiday. "At Pocketpair, we believe such a historic occasion deserves our full attention."

From November 19 to November 23, "all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto 6" at Pocketpair will be "excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to undertake a business trip to Vice City." Technically, since that time spans a weekend, it's only really granting three days of holiday time. But, you know, who's counting?

The studio also made sure to note that work is proceeding on updates for Palworld and Craftopia, which are "expected to be carried out as scheduled," presumably in an effort to preempt anyone who might be reaching for their torches and pitchforks.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever players in Australia and New Zealand are struggling to get sunlight, and not for the usual MMO reasons
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.
body: But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!
points: World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.
